# dlaqge

> Scales a general rectangular matrix, using row and column scaling factors computed by sgeequ.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaqge from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaqge';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaqge(
    order,
    M, N,
    A, LDA,
    r, strideR,
    c, strideC,
    rowcnd, colcnd, amax,
    equed
) → Float64Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | the number of rows of the matrix A. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | the number of columns of the matrix A. |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `max( M, 1 ) × N` |  | on entry, the M by N matrix A. On exit, the equilibrated matrix. |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `A` |
| `r` | `Float64Array` | in | `M` |  | the row scale factors for A. |
| ↳ `strideR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `r` |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | the column scale factors for A. |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `c` |
| `rowcnd` | `number` | in |  |  | ratio of the smallest R(i) to the largest R(i). |
| `colcnd` | `number` | in |  |  | ratio of the smallest C(i) to the largest C(i). |
| `amax` | `number` | in |  |  | absolute value of largest matrix entry. |
| `equed` | `Array.<string>` | out |  |  | specifies the form of equilibration that was done. `'none'`: No equilibration `'row'`: Row equilibration, i.e., A has been premultiplied by diag(R). `'column'`: Column equilibration, i.e., A has been postmultiplied by diag(C). `'both'`: Both row and column equilibration, i.e., A has been replaced by diag(R) * A * diag(C). |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the M by N matrix A. On exit, the equilibrated matrix. See `EQUED` for the form of the equilibrated matrix.
- `r`: The row scale factors for A.
- `c`: The column scale factors for A.
- `rowcnd`: Ratio of the smallest `R(i)` to the largest `R(i)`.
- `colcnd`: Ratio of the smallest `C(i)` to the largest `C(i)`.
- `amax`: Absolute value of largest matrix entry.
- `equed`: Specifies the form of equilibration that was done.

  -   `= 'N'`: No equilibration
  -   `= 'R'`: Row equilibration, i.e., A has been premultiplied by diag(R).
  -   `= 'C'`: Column equilibration, i.e., A has been postmultiplied by diag(C).
  -   `= 'B'`: Both row and column equilibration, i.e., A has been replaced by $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(C)$.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `A`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaqge.ndarray(
    M, N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    r, strideR, offsetR,
    c, strideC, offsetC,
    rowcnd, colcnd, amax,
    equed
) → Float64Array
```

Equilibrates a general M-by-N matrix A using the row and column scaling.
factors in the vectors R and C.

Returns 'N' (no equilibration), 'R' (row only), 'C' (column only),
or 'B' (both row and column).

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of rows of A |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of columns of A |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `max( M, 1 ) × N` |  | input/output M-by-N matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for A |
| `r` | `Float64Array` | in | `M` |  | row scale factors, length M |
| ↳ `strideR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for r |
| ↳ `offsetR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for r |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | column scale factors, length N |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for c |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for c |
| `rowcnd` | `number` | in |  |  | ratio of smallest to largest R(i) |
| `colcnd` | `number` | in |  |  | ratio of smallest to largest C(i) |
| `amax` | `number` | in |  |  | absolute value of largest matrix entry |
| `equed` | `Array.<string>` | out |  |  | specifies the form of equilibration that was done. `'none'`: No equilibration `'row'`: Row equilibration, i.e., A has been premultiplied by diag(R). `'column'`: Column equilibration, i.e., A has been postmultiplied by diag(C). `'both'`: Both row and column equilibration, i.e., A has been replaced by diag(R) * A * diag(C). |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the M by N matrix A. On exit, the equilibrated matrix. See `EQUED` for the form of the equilibrated matrix.
- `r`: The row scale factors for A.
- `c`: The column scale factors for A.
- `rowcnd`: Ratio of the smallest `R(i)` to the largest `R(i)`.
- `colcnd`: Ratio of the smallest `C(i)` to the largest `C(i)`.
- `amax`: Absolute value of largest matrix entry.
- `equed`: Specifies the form of equilibration that was done.

  -   `= 'N'`: No equilibration
  -   `= 'R'`: Row equilibration, i.e., A has been premultiplied by diag(R).
  -   `= 'C'`: Column equilibration, i.e., A has been postmultiplied by diag(C).
  -   `= 'B'`: Both row and column equilibration, i.e., A has been replaced by $\operatorname{diag}(R) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(C)$.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `A`

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlaqge()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAQGE`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlaqge.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dlaqge from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaqge';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const r = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const c = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
const equed = [ '' ];
let out = dlaqge( 'column-major', N, N, A, N, r, 1, c, 1, 1, 1, 1, equed );
console.log( out, equed[ 0 ] );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dlaqge.ndarray( N, N, A, N, 1, 0, r, 1, 0, c, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, equed );
console.log( out, equed[ 0 ] );
```

</section>
